Episode 04 · Case File 11-B

THE PHANTOM COLLISION

A cargo cart that wasn't on camera. A security report that says it was parked. The laws of momentum tell another story.

Conservation of momentumImpulseElastic vs inelasticKinetic energyGrades 9–12
CHAPTER 1

CHAPTER 01 · THE MISSION

Was B2 really parked?

The security report says B2 was standing still when A1 hit it. After the latches locked, the two carts rolled right together at +2.40 m/s. Predict whether the report can be true before you calculate.

CHAPTER 02 · THE EVIDENCE

Reconstruct the phantom

Mass of A1600 kg
A1 before (vA,i)+8.0 m/s
Mass of B2400 kg
Both after (vf)+2.40 m/s

The carts latch together. The collision lasts only milliseconds, so the total momentum of the two carts just before and just after is the same. Right is positive, left is negative.

mAvA,i + mBvB,i = (mA + mB)vf
CHAPTER 03 · YOUR PHYSICS

Find the impact signature

Now you know B2's velocity. Find the impulse on B2 and the kinetic energy the carts lost when they latched. Momentum is conserved in this collision; kinetic energy does not have to be.

JB = mB(vf − vB,i)  ·  K = ½mv²  ·  KE lost = Kbefore − Kafter
CHAPTER 04 · CHOOSE THE REPLAY

Latch or spring?

The engineers will replay the collision on a test track: same carts, same starting velocities (A1 at +8.0 m/s, B2 at −6.0 m/s). You choose the hardware. Predict, then calculate both final velocities to run the replay.

CHAPTER 05 · THE PIER-END ARRESTOR

Stop the runaway cart

In the spring replay, B2 (400 kg) leaves the collision at +10.8 m/s, heading for the end of the causeway. There are only 5.2 m of track before the pier edge. Design an arrestor that stops B2 in time, without going over the force limit, and with enough heat-sink modules to absorb its kinetic energy. Assume a constant braking force that starts immediately.

Mass of B2400 kg
Incoming vi+10.8 m/s
Max average force5,000 N
Track left5.2 m
Favg = |Δp| / Δt  ·  Δx = ½(vi + vf)Δt  ·  K = ½mvi²
Each heat-sink module absorbs 8,000 J and adds 90 kg. The mount holds at most 270 kg of modules.
1 · Minimum stopping time2 · Approved design

Step 1 · Minimum safe stopping time

What is the shortest stopping time that keeps the average force at or below 5,000 N? If you round, round to a safe value.
